manifest.title: AX Engine vs MLXcel: Qwen 3.6 Loss Review and Fix
manifest.description: Technical diagnosis and validated fix for the Qwen 3.6 27B 4-bit long-prompt decode loss, with historical benchmark context and promotion gates.

blocks.body:
# AX Engine vs MLXcel: Qwen 3.6 Loss Review and Fix

Technical review, controlled route A/B, implementation, and validation for the Apple M3 Max Qwen 3.6 27B 4-bit decode loss.

## Technical summary

**The 27B 4-bit loss is fixed.** The controlled route A/B isolated AX's default custom Qwen dense-FFN gate/up plus down 4-bit Metal matvec path as the causal regression for the model's 64-layer, 5120 → 17408 dense FFN geometry. With the custom route active, decode measured **19.33 tok/s median** and a **16.37% spread** across three repetitions. Disabling it and using MLX's split quantized-matmul FFN measured **22.74 tok/s** with a **2.94% spread**. All repetitions emitted the same 256 token IDs.

The implementation now bypasses the custom route only for that exact dense geometry. The patched default completed two warmups and five measured repetitions at **22.54 tok/s median**, a **2.98% spread**, and **+3.03% first-to-last drift**. That is **+19.9%** versus the overnight MLXcel 18.8 tok/s reference and **+35.0%** versus the reported AX 16.7 tok/s row. A separate route/provenance smoke explicitly forced the custom-kernel flag on; server telemetry still recorded zero attempts and zero hits, confirming the geometry guard—not an inherited kill switch—selected the faster path.

The original row was still methodologically confounded by fixed run order, three repetitions, and background load. Those weaknesses explain why its exact −11.2% effect size was not trustworthy, but they no longer prevent root-cause attribution: the route A/B and patched replication identify an AX-controlled performance defect. AX still won 7 of 8 overnight scenarios, with geometric-mean advantages of **11.1% decode**, **6.6% effective prefill**, and **6.9% TTFT** before this fix.

## Controlled FFN route A/B identifies the regression

Both arms used the same exact 2,048-token random prompt (`a7c9e08d17d2…`), direct greedy decode, 256 generated tokens, disabled prefix reuse, one warmup, three measurements, and five-second cooldowns. The custom route produced 64 gate/up kernel attempts and hits per request and tailed from 19.87 to 16.70 tok/s. The MLX split-FFN arm produced zero custom attempts, held between 22.28 and 22.95 tok/s, reduced accumulated asynchronous-evaluation time, and increased effective bandwidth from 310.3 to 365.0 GB/s at the median.

The final patched run strengthened the protocol to two warmups, five measurements, 15-second cooldowns, and per-repetition load gates. It reproduced the split-route result at 22.54 tok/s with stable classification. Because the A/B and patched arms emitted byte-identical token sequences, the change affects execution cost rather than model semantics.

## Historical benchmark context

The first overnight AX repetition exactly matched MLXcel at 18.6 tok/s; separation appeared only in later AX repetitions. The controlled route A/B now explains why the AX custom FFN path could both match the reference initially and then tail under changing Metal state. Because the overnight harness ran AX before MLXcel for each model, then ran the 512-target rows before the 2K rows, its exact −11.2% effect size remains confounded even though the underlying AX route regression is real.

### Only one loss is material

The 35B-A3B 4-bit p512 effective-prefill/TTFT dip is 2.3%, or about 15 ms. It is a low-confidence three-repetition difference: the sibling 35B-A3B 6-bit p512 AX row contained a 1.022 s TTFT outlier between 0.580 s and 0.590 s. AX still won that 35B 4-bit cell's decode comparison by 19.5%.

## Earlier fixed-prompt diagnostics localized where to look

The first direct-policy diagnostic held the raw 2,048-token prompt, random seed, 256 generated token IDs, KV geometry, and process memory constant. Decode fell 12.8% from repetition 1 to 5. Over the same interval, MLX asynchronous-evaluation wall time rose 16.0%, from 12.70 s to 14.74 s, while AX forward/bookkeeping time stayed near 1.0 s. At the slow tail, asynchronous evaluation accounted for 93.5% of decode wall time.

The default n-gram process produced zero draft attempts and zero accepted tokens, so speculation could not explain the loss. A 15-second-cooldown run recovered from 15.9 to 18.4 tok/s as host load fell. Those observations correctly localized the problem to the evaluated op stream and its sensitivity to Metal state, but only the later route A/B separated the custom FFN matvec path from the MLX split-FFN fallback.

## Scope and metric definitions

The completed serving matrix covers four checkpoints—27B dense-hybrid and 35B-A3B mixture-of-experts, each at 4-bit and 6-bit—at nominal 512- and 2,048-token prompt targets. Every cell generated 256 tokens through streaming `/v1/chat/completions` with temperature 0.

**TTFT** is client request-send to first content or reasoning chunk. **Effective prefill throughput** is the engine-reported prompt-token count divided by client-observed TTFT. **Decode throughput** is `(completion tokens - 1) / (last content chunk time - first content chunk time)`. A positive comparison means AX is faster; an AX loss is reported as `(AX / MLXcel - 1) × 100%`. **Relative spread** is `(maximum − minimum) / median × 100%`; **drift** is `(last / first − 1) × 100%`.

The two engines' overnight chat templates differed by roughly five prompt tokens, so that comparison is close but not token-identical. The route A/B and patched AX runs use an exact 2,048-token raw prompt with SHA-256 `a7c9e08d17d246…`, direct greedy decode, and captured output token IDs. The 18.8 tok/s MLXcel value is therefore a historical serving reference, not a same-process fixed-token control.

## Methodology and evidence chain

The overnight harness completed all 48 measurements with no request errors: 4 models × 2 prompt targets × 2 engines × 3 repetitions. It used fresh deterministic prompts per target/repetition, two-second gaps between repetitions, and five-second gaps between server processes. Execution order was model → engine (AX first) → prompt target (512 first).

The route A/B used the repository inference-stack harness against the current release build with direct AX decode, one warmup, three measured repetitions, a fixed 2,048-token prompt, five-second cooldowns, prefix reuse disabled, and output-ID capture. Arm A explicitly enabled the custom Qwen dense-FFN Metal matvec route; arm B explicitly disabled it. The patched validation used two warmups, five measured repetitions, 15-second cooldowns, and per-repetition gates of one-minute load ≤6 and top-process CPU ≤120%. The gate delayed samples during observed `fseventsd` and VM spikes. Host activity was not equivalent to an idle boot, but the run remained stable and records all conditions.

A final one-measurement smoke explicitly enabled the custom route after the patch. It is correctness/provenance evidence only: the artifact records both the configured and explicit-enable flags as true, while server telemetry records zero route attempts/hits. This proves the model-geometry guard executes before the custom kernel. Its single throughput sample is excluded because the host did not meet the repeated-run stability conditions.

## Limitations, uncertainty, and robustness

- The overnight comparison has only three repetitions, fixed engine order, fixed prompt-length order, short cooldowns, no fresh boot, and no captured output token IDs. Its −11.2% effect size remains exploratory.
- Controlled runs diagnose AX only; there is no matched fixed-token MLXcel trace in the same process-order design. The patched +19.9% comparison uses the overnight MLXcel median as a historical reference.
- The A/B arms were sequential rather than randomized. The effect is nevertheless replicated across the explicit custom-on tail, stable explicit custom-off measurements, and the patched default result. The forced-on smoke separately confirms guard selection and identical output IDs; its throughput is not used.
- The patched run met the repetition and stability gates but ran from a dirty development tree by design and skipped the in-run `mlx_lm` reference. It is decision-grade implementation evidence, not a public release-claim artifact.
- The geometry guard is intentionally exact. It preserves the measured Qwen3.5-9B custom-kernel win and cannot match the Qwen3.6-35B-A3B configuration, but the complete 27B/35B 4-bit/6-bit serving matrix should still be rerun before release.
- Current evidence identifies the combined custom gate/up plus matching down-kernel route. It does not apportion the regression between the two kernels.

## Ranked improvement plan

**1. Keep the exact 27B geometry and quantization guard.** The patch clears the target-cell promotion thresholds: +16.6% versus the custom-route diagnostic median, 2.98% spread, 3.03% drift, and byte-identical output. The exception is restricted to 4-bit/group-64; do not disable the route globally because the smaller Qwen3.5-9B geometry has a measured 3–4% custom-kernel gain.

**2. Rerun the complete serving matrix before release.** Alternate engine order, use two warmups plus at least five measurements, retain 15-second cooldowns and load gates, capture output IDs where the engines expose comparable tokens, and bind the measured binary SHA. Require no regression over 2% in the other seven scenarios.

**3. Split-profile gate/up versus down only if broader shape coverage is needed.** The current evidence attributes the combined custom FFN route. A shape sweep with paired kernel-level timing can determine whether a tuned threshold or revised kernel should replace the exact deny rule. Until then, the narrow guard minimizes regression risk.

**4. Keep upstream MLX-main evaluation as a separate opportunity.** Post-0.32 changes may add another 2–5% or reduce variance, but they are no longer required to close this loss. Test them only after the patched release baseline is established.

**5. Preserve the benchmark provenance fix.** The harness now records configured default-on state separately from an explicit CLI override and declares server route telemetry authoritative. Raw runs in this review predate that metadata fix, so their route telemetry—not the old top-level boolean—determines whether the kernel executed.

### Decision gates

The patch passes the target-cell gates: more than 3% gain, drift below 5%, spread below 5%, and byte-identical greedy output. Release promotion still requires the other seven serving scenarios to remain within 2% and a clean, immutable binary artifact. Treat a fresh-boot, alternating-order full-matrix rerun as the publication result; use the overnight MLXcel median only as historical context.

## Further questions

1. Does the complete alternating-order 27B/35B matrix confirm no regression outside the fixed cell?
2. Which half of the combined route—gate/up+SwiGLU or down projection—causes the large-geometry regression?
3. Where is the shape crossover between the Qwen3.5-9B win at 4096 → 12288 and the Qwen3.6-27B loss at 5120 → 17408?
4. Can the harness bind an immutable binary build SHA and distinguish explicit fast-path flags from effective server routes?
5. Does current MLX main add a separate gain after this AX-controlled loss is removed?

sources.label: Qwen 27B fixed-prompt FFN route A/B and patched validation

query.description: Read each AX inference-stack artifact, select the direct AX result, and compare decode median, spread, drift, route telemetry, and output IDs.
query.sql:
WITH route_rows AS (
  SELECT 'Custom fused route (A)' AS configuration, result
  FROM read_json_auto('benchmarks/results/serving/single-client-mlxcel/2026-08-05-qwen36-27b-35b/improvement/ffn-fused-a.json'), UNNEST(results) AS t(result)
  WHERE result.engine = 'ax_engine_mlx'
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'MLX split FFN (B)' AS configuration, result
  FROM read_json_auto('benchmarks/results/serving/single-client-mlxcel/2026-08-05-qwen36-27b-35b/improvement/ffn-mlx-b.json'), UNNEST(results) AS t(result)
  WHERE result.engine = 'ax_engine_mlx'
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'Patched default' AS configuration, result
  FROM read_json_auto('benchmarks/results/serving/single-client-mlxcel/2026-08-05-qwen36-27b-35b/improvement/patched-default-final.json'), UNNEST(results) AS t(result)
  WHERE result.engine = 'ax_engine_mlx'
)
SELECT
  configuration,
  result.decode_tok_s.median AS median_decode_tok_s,
  result.run_stability.relative_spread_pct AS relative_spread_pct,
  result.run_stability.last_vs_first_pct AS drift_pct,
  result.run_stability.trial_count AS repetitions
FROM route_rows
ORDER BY median_decode_tok_s DESC;
filters: 256 generated tokens with prefix reuse disabled
metric_definitions: Decode median is the median of measured decode_tok_s trials.
Relative spread is (max - min) / median × 100%.
Drift is (last / first - 1) × 100%.
Historical MLXcel comparison uses the overnight 18.8 tok/s median and is not part of the fixed-token route A/B.

sources.label: Completed AX Engine vs MLXcel serving benchmark

query.description: Flatten the completed benchmark's reviewed per-repetition measurements; report metrics are medians and paired ratios derived from these rows.
query.sql:
WITH artifact AS (
  SELECT *
  FROM read_json_auto('benchmarks/results/serving/single-client-mlxcel/2026-08-05-qwen36-27b-35b/benchmark.json')
), measurement_rows AS (
  SELECT UNNEST(measurements) AS measurement
  FROM artifact
)
SELECT
  measurement.engine AS engine,
  measurement.model AS model,
  measurement.prompt_target AS prompt_target,
  measurement.rep + 1 AS repetition,
  measurement.prompt_tokens AS prompt_tokens,
  measurement.completion_tokens AS completion_tokens,
  measurement.ttft_s AS ttft_s,
  measurement.prefill_tps AS effective_prefill_tok_s,
  measurement.decode_tps AS decode_tok_s
FROM measurement_rows
ORDER BY model, engine, prompt_target, repetition;
filters: Apple M3 Max serving run on 2026-08-05
metric_definitions: Cell values are medians across three repetitions.
AX delta is (AX median / MLXcel median - 1) × 100%.
Geometric-mean comparisons use the eight paired model, quantization, and prompt-target scenarios.

sources.label: Fixed-prompt AX direct versus n-gram-policy diagnostic

query.description: Flatten the fixed-prompt diagnostic's direct AX repetitions and selected timing telemetry.
query.sql:
WITH artifact AS (
  SELECT *
  FROM read_json_auto('benchmarks/results/serving/single-client-mlxcel/2026-08-05-qwen36-27b-35b/diagnostics/27b4-p2048-fixed-prompt-policy-ab.json')
), direct_row AS (
  SELECT result
  FROM artifact, UNNEST(results) AS t(result)
  WHERE result.engine = 'ax_engine_mlx'
), trial_rows AS (
  SELECT ROW_NUMBER() OVER () AS repetition, trial
  FROM direct_row, UNNEST(result.trials) AS t(trial)
)
SELECT
  repetition,
  trial.decode_tok_s AS decode_tok_s,
  trial.prefill_tok_s AS prefill_tok_s,
  trial.ax_mlx_telemetry.ax_mlx_direct_pipeline_async_eval_wall_us / 1000.0 AS async_eval_ms,
  trial.ax_mlx_telemetry.ax_mlx_direct_pipeline_forward_wall_us / 1000.0 AS forward_ms,
  trial.ax_mlx_telemetry.ax_mlx_kv_capacity_kib / 1024.0 AS kv_capacity_mib,
  trial.peak_memory_gb AS process_rss_gib
FROM trial_rows
ORDER BY repetition;
filters: Two warmups, five measurements, two-second cooldown
metric_definitions: Async eval wall is MLX asynchronous graph-evaluation time accumulated by AX telemetry.
Forward wall is AX forward and graph/bookkeeping time.
First-to-last drift is (repetition 5 / repetition 1 - 1) × 100%.

FROM (VALUES
